indian.headline: Indian markets rallied on festive spending strength and Reliance's stellar Q2, adding ₹6 lakh crore.
indian.lead: Indian markets rallied on festive spending strength and Reliance's stellar Q2, adding ₹6 lakh crore.
indian.brief: Sensex surged 1.66% and Nifty 50 climbed 1.68% on robust consumption signals and corporate earnings beats.
why: UPI crossed ₹1 lakh crore average daily transactions in October and processed ₹31.53 lakh crore monthly (up 16% YoY), signalling strong digital payments and festive spending momentum that lifted consumption-linked sectors.
Reliance Industries' Q2 profit jumped 41% YoY to ₹25,548 crore, beating estimates and driving the stock 6% higher, pulling energy and large-cap indices up.
GST collections hit a record ₹2.32 lakh crore in October, up 22.9% YoY, confirming robust underlying economic activity that outpaced inflation and high interest rates.
Energy sector surged 3.9% and Metals +3.2% on falling oil prices mentioned as a key rally driver, offsetting modest FII selling pressure.
indian.narrative:
Indian equities delivered a strong rally on 2 November 2026, with the Sensex jumping over 1,000 points to cross fresh highs and the Nifty 50 breaking above 23,300. The market added ₹6 lakh crore in value in under an hour, driven by a confluence of positive data: UPI transactions crossed ₹1 lakh crore daily for the first time, GST collections hit an all-time monthly high of ₹2.32 lakh crore (up 22.9% YoY), and Reliance Industries posted a 41% profit jump in Q2 earnings.

The rally was broad-based, with energy stocks (+3.9%), metals (+3.2%), and autos (+1.3%) leading gainers. Falling oil prices emerged as a structural tailwind. However, not all sectors participated: pharma and IT slipped into red territory, while banking gains remained modest at +0.6% despite the headline euphoria. Foreign institutional investors continued their 2026 retreat, having sold nearly ₹3 lakh crore of Indian equities so far this year, but domestic momentum from festive season consumption and robust Q2 corporate earnings proved strong enough to override the outflow headwind.

tiles.label: Global cues
tiles.sub: Falling oil prices aided rally; U.S. election headlines present but no direct market impact yet.

tiles.label: FII activity
tiles.sub: Nearly ₹3 lakh crore sold by FIIs in 2026; selling pressure ongoing despite domestic strength.

tiles.label: Crude oil
tiles.sub: Lower oil prices cited as key rally driver, benefiting energy stocks and import costs.

indian.watch: Monitor FII flows and Q2 earnings trajectory; watch if consumption strength (UPI, GST) sustains beyond festive season.

us.headline: US markets tumbled as Big Tech earnings worries and high debt levels weighed heavily on sentiment.
us.lead: US markets tumbled as Big Tech earnings worries and high debt levels weighed heavily on sentiment.
us.brief: S&P 500 fell 1.82%, Nasdaq slid 2.86%, and Dow dropped 1.09%, with tech stocks taking the hardest hit at -4.9%.
why: Apple's earnings call under new CEO John Ternus sparked concern over high memory costs and weak consumer demand in Big Tech.
Magnificent Seven companies' total debt surged to $578 billion since 2023—a 45% rise—raising questions about leverage and sustainability.
Tech sector weakness (-4.9%) dragged the broader market lower despite Energy (+1.9%) and Healthcare (+0.5%) gains.
us.narrative:
US stock markets closed lower on November 2 as investors reassessed Big Tech's earnings trajectory and balance sheet health. The Nasdaq bore the brunt, declining 2.86%, while the S&P 500 and Dow fell 1.82% and 1.09% respectively. Tech stocks plummeted 4.9%—the day's worst performer—as Apple reported results under newly installed CEO John Ternus amid elevated memory costs and softening consumer spending. The weakness reflected broader unease over the sector's debt burden: Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, and Tesla have nearly doubled combined borrowing to $578 billion since 2023, driven largely by AI infrastructure investments.

Meanwhile, AI enthusiasm remained a bright spot globally. OpenAI's Sam Altman visited South Korea to deepen chip and data center partnerships with Samsung and SK Group, while Seoul announced a record 2027 budget allocating 4.7 trillion won toward building a world-class sovereign AI model. Energy stocks gained 1.9% and Financials held relatively steady at -0.8%, suggesting selective strength outside the tech downturn. The day underscored a key tension for retail investors: while AI investment fever continues internationally, US market leaders face near-term pressure from rising costs and softer demand.

tiles.label: Big mover
tiles.sub: New CEO John Ternus faces high memory costs and weak demand.

tiles.label: Key data
tiles.sub: Magnificent Seven tech firms' combined borrowing up 45% since 2023.

tiles.label: Backdrop
tiles.sub: But AI momentum stays alive in South Korea and chip partnerships.

us.watch: Monitor Apple's earnings guidance and tech sector sentiment shifts as Q3 results season unfolds this week.
